articles.title: Make a Difference Awards NI: Belfast 'hidden gem' among finalists
articles.summary: Annadale Community Garden Group is one of four groups or individuals in the running for this year's Make a Difference Awards NI.
articles.body:
From a lifeless strip of grass to a blossoming garden, Annadale Community Centre's grounds have received a glow up over the past year, becoming a "hidden gem" for all to enjoy.

The volunteer group has now been recognised for its contribution to the local area, receiving a nomination for the BBC Make a Difference Awards .

Annadale Community Centre Gardening Group meets every Tuesday and will celebrate its first birthday in September.

Residents say the space has not only improved the local environment but has also created a welcoming community hub where people can learn new skills, share ideas and support each other through life's challenges.

Kirstie Rowan has been involved since the beginning and is proud of the journey the group has been on, which has been full of "lovely big changes".

"We started with the grass, unwanted containers and the polytunnel and now we have all of this – we've got the pond, tree bed and vegetables as well," she explained.

"Every week when we come down there's always more growth, more flowers, new flowers, it really is beautiful.

"Some of us don't work so this gets us out of the house weekly and even if we come, we aren't expected to do anything, its just nice to be here with everyone."

For Fayth Duffy, being part of the group has been a "game changer" for her after recently moving to the area.

"I was really finding it hard to put down roots and meet friends because when your kids get a bit older you're not meeting the mums at the gate, you're not getting out to the other places such as toddler groups," she said.

"We've all become such good friends, we go for coffee together sometimes afterwards and support each other, we'll ring each other to make sure we are all here."

For local resident Larry Andrews the group has been a refuge following the death of his wife last year.

"I came here for a bit of company, my daughter found it on WhatsApp and I've been coming since September last year," he said.

The 87-year-old former butcher has made new friends through the group.

"It's good to meet different people and have a yarn with them… It's amazing the number of people you do find," he added.

Amber Jennings works with the group and is on hand with gardening tips and advice.

"It means a lot to be nominated for this award - I feel like this is such a hidden gem on the Ormeau Road for people to retreat to on a Tuesday morning and learn how to garden with those in the community," she said.

The primary goal of the group is to "improve the wellbeing of people in the area".

Jennings has seen first hand the difference the garden has made to members.

"It's been a really uplifting experience for all involved, having that routine, knowing you're outside and being with people in your community," she added.

It is awarded to an individual or group who improve or conserve their local environment.

Annadale Community Centre Garden Group is one of four finalists in the category, along with:

Daniel McAfee - Ballycastle, a wildlife volunteer and member of the Glens Red Squirrel Group where he shares his knowledge through school visits, talks and guided nature walks

Alannah Agnew - Cookstown , a passionate member and chairperson of her school eco team. She has led assemblies on climate change, littering and healthy eating, while helping her school achieve its sixth Green Flag award

Eco Rangers NI - Carrickfergus, a community litter-picking group that clears litter year-round, supports community events and helps young people with awards such as the Duke of Edinburgh Award

Overall winners will be announced live on Vinny and Cate's BBC Radio Ulster show on Friday 25 September.

articles.title: Solheim Cup: Chance to regain trophy offers 'extra incentive' says wildcard Leona Maguire
articles.summary: Ireland's Leona Maguire says the opportunity for Europe to reclaim the Solheim Cup from the United States offers added incentive before the contest in the Netherlands in September.
articles.body:
Ireland's Leona Maguire says the opportunity to regain the Solheim Cup offers an "extra incentive" for Team Europe as they prepare to face the United States at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands next month.

Maguire was part of the team which contested the 2024 edition as the US ran out 15.5-12.5 winners in Virginia.

The 31-year-old also participated in Europe's victory on Ohio in 2021 and the drawn encounter in Andalusia, which saw the Europeans retain the trophy.

Captain Anna Nordqvist chose Maguire as one of two wildcard picks for this year's event in Cromvoirt from 11-13 September.

Maguire will compete in the Women's Irish Open at the K Club in County Kildare this week, her last competitive action before the team contest in the Netherlands.

"Hopefully have a great week here [at the Irish Open] and then a week off to recharge and go again for the Solheim," Maguire told BBC Sport.

"Solheim's a special event every two years and a home Solheim is even more special.

"We've got a young team this year, an exciting team and looking forward to getting over to the Netherlands for that."

'Once you're part of one, you don't want to miss any more'

The 31-year-old became the first Irish player to represent Europe in the competition when she was selected for the 2021 version and broke the all-time rookie points record for either the Solheim Cup or Ryder Cup with a contribution of 4.5 points as the away team triumphed 15-13.

The County Cavan woman's overall individual record in the competition after also taking part in the two subsequent editions reads eight wins, one half and three defeats.

"It's one of my favourite events. It's a team event which we don't get to do very often and matchplay which I love," she explained.

"I think once you're part of one Solheim, the same as the Ryder Cup, you don't want to miss any more.

"It's competitive, there's no money on the line, it's all just for pride and all the rest. You're doing whatever you can to help your teammates and the team.

"We obviously lost the last one so there's an extra incentive to try and bring it back this time."

Maguire, a two-time winner on the LPGA Tour and a one-time victor on the Ladies European Tour, hopes the backing of home supporters can help Europe reclaim the trophy at the 20th running of the event.

"Home support always helps as well. There was massive Irish support in Spain two times ago so hopefully a few Irish will maybe make the trip to Holland."

articles.title: PGA Tour CEO responds after Callaway, Good Good Golf apologize for ad in which a man shoves a woman to the ground over a driver
articles.summary: Callaway said it never should have approved the ad in the first place.
articles.body:
Callaway and Good Good Golf are scrambling to apologize after a joint ad backfired in a major way. The now-deleted ad — which featured a man shoving a woman to the ground over a driver — drew intense criticism for making light of domestic violence.

Good Good Golf originally posted the video Friday. A day later, however, the video was deleted and the company released a statement apologizing for it.

The ad was for a co-branded driver with Callaway. In it, Good Good Golf co-founder Garrett Clark runs over and shoves content creator Alexis Miestowski to the ground before she can touch Clark's driver. Clark then sinisterly utters, "Do not touch my new driver" as Miestowski lays on the ground.

Here's the now-deleted ad in case that description doesn't sound worrisome enough:

Early Tuesday, Callaway responded, putting out a lengthy statement apologizing for the video being approved and released.

In the statement, Callaway clarified that the video was produced by Good Good Golf, but was approved by Callaway before it was posted. "That approval should never have happened," the post stated.

Callaway clarified it is "unequivocally against discrimination, domestic violence, or threatening behavior of any kind." The company also announced it was launching internal and external investigations and said it has already changed its approval process to ensure "this will never happen again."

PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp was asked about the video on Tuesday ahead of the Tour Championship. The Tour recently partnered with Good Good, and will host the Good Good Championship in Austin later this fall.

"I think what we saw was concerning, is clearly not aligned with PGA Tour values," Rolapp said. "We take it very seriously. I think their initial response was disappointing. It was a bit defensive and late. "But I think the responses are getting better. I think we've seen some things this morning, we've had some conversations with them, so we'll continue to monitor and work with them going forward. But no, we were disappointed with what we saw."

"I think what we saw was concerning, is clearly not aligned with PGA Tour values," Rolapp said. "We take it very seriously. I think their initial response was disappointing. It was a bit defensive and late.

"But I think the responses are getting better. I think we've seen some things this morning, we've had some conversations with them, so we'll continue to monitor and work with them going forward. But no, we were disappointed with what we saw."

Good Good started as a YouTube channel, but eventually grew into a golf sponsor. The company is the title sponsor of the Good Good Golf Championship, which will take place in November.

As a result of the ad and the backlash that ensued, the Gold Channel announced on Tuesday night that it was postponing the debut of its "Big Break" reboot. One of the show's sponsors, reportedly retailer Golf Galaxy, asked to have its branding removed from the series. The rebood of the series was titled "Big Break x Good Good."

articles.title: Warriors reportedly sign $37M 11-year veteran, 40% 3-point shooter to pair with Steph Curry
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors have had a disappoint offseason. On Tuesday, they made a huge signing for a journeyman in the league.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors are entering the latter stages of Steph Curry and Draymond Green 's careers, yet they have continued to avoid making any major acquisitions. That has left many fans frustrated with what the organization has done this summer and concerned about the team's future.

At the beginning of free agency, the Warriors were linked to both LeBron James and Anthony Davis . Instead of landing either superstar, Golden State has largely relied on familiar faces who have previously played for the franchise.

"The Warriors are officially running it back despite missing the playoffs last season. Golden State re-signed Draymond Green, Kristaps Porzingis , Al Horford , De'Anthony Melton, and Gary Payton II this summer," NBA writer Jake Weinbach posted.

On Tuesday, Golden State finally broke that pattern by signing a guard who should provide a major boost to its bench in Brandon Williams .

"The Golden State Warriors are signing free agent guard Brandon Williams to a one-year, $2.6 million minimum contract, agents Derek Lafayette and Curtis Lawrence told ESPN's Shams Charania on Tuesday. Williams is the team's first outside acquisition in what has been an otherwise stable offseason, providing needed perimeter bench scoring and speed for a reserve unit that often lacked it last season," ESPN's Anthony Slater wrote.

However, that was not the only move Golden State made Tuesday. The Warriors also signed veteran forward Georges Niang to help round out the roster.

"Free agent forward Georges Niang has agreed to a one-year, $3.9 million deal with the Golden State Warriors, Mark Bartelstein and Andy Shiffman of Priority Sports tell ESPN. Niang -- a career 40% 3-point shooter -- enters his 11th NBA season after missing 2025-26 due to injury," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote.

This is a significant addition for the Warriors, as Niang should become an important piece off the bench and could potentially see an expanded role while Jimmy Butler recovers. His ability to knock down shots from deep should create more floor spacing for an offense that relies heavily on perimeter shooting.

Niang has made $37 million throughout his 11-year NBA career. He is joining Golden State on a relatively small contract, making this a low-risk addition for the Warriors. For Golden State, adding Niang is a solid way to round out the roster heading into the upcoming season.

articles.title: Callaway apologises after golf ad slammed for depicting domestic violence
articles.summary: The advert, which was released online last week before being pulled, prompted calls for a boycott of Callaway products.
articles.body:
Golf equipment giant Callaway has issued an apology, although largely in vain, after facing an immense backlash for an advertisement depicting violence against women, which has since been removed.

The commercial, which was released online last week before being pulled, showed a male golfer shoving a female player to the ground when she reaches for his new driver, and prompted calls for a boycott of Callaway products.

Callaway issued an apology for the advertisement, and Callaway chief executive Chip Brewer said in a statement on Tuesday that the company had launched an investigation into how the advertisement — produced by golf media firm Good Good Golf — had been approved.

“Last week Good Good Golf and Callaway posted a video to promote a co-branded driver,” Brewer said in a statement.

“While the video was produced by Good Good, it was approved by Callaway prior to posting. That approval should never have happened. Mistakes were made and we are taking the matter very seriously.

“As we deal with the consequences of our mistake and complete our investigations, I want to make it clear that we sincerely apologize for the video.

“The content was inappropriate and does not reflect our values. To be clear: we are unequivocally against discrimination, domestic violence or threatening behaviour of any kind … I assure you we will learn from this and do better.”

The online advertisement showed Good Good cofounder Garrett Clark shoving Epson Tour professional player Alexis Miestowski to the ground when she attempted to reach for his driver, before warning her: “Do not touch my new driver.”

Good Good Golf, which centres its business around a successful YouTube channel aimed at bringing a younger audience to the sport, had already apologised for the controversial advertisement.

“We posted a video to our channels that ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand,” Good Good said in a statement.

“We have since taken that content down. And sincerely apologize. Good Good has always stood for making the game of golf more inclusive to all, and we will continue to ensure that is our mission moving forward.”

Good Good’s rise will see the company be the title sponsor for the PGA Tour’s inaugural Good Good Championship in Austin, Texas in November.

PGA Tour chief executive Brian Rolapp said on Tuesday the circuit was dismayed by the advertisement and Good Good’s handling of the controversy.

“I think what we saw was concerning, is clearly not aligned with PGA Tour values. We take it very seriously,” Rolapp said.

“I think their initial response was disappointing. It was a bit defensive and late.

“But I think the responses are getting better. We’ve seen some things this morning, we’ve had some conversations with them, so we’ll continue to monitor and work with them going forward. But no, we were disappointed with what we saw.”

Online criticism has been aimed at representation, accountability, and decision-making surrounding the advertisement, in addition to domestic violence being promoted.

Social media users have questioned how the advertisement was greenlit to begin with, with many infuriated that it was removed only after backlash and not because either company realised how controversial it was.

One woman golfer on social media said the advertisement was a significant setback for women looking to break into the male-dominated sport, with many emphasising that the apologies from Callaway and Good Good Golf did not come across as genuine.

Several Callaway customers publicly renounced their loyalty to the brand after being appalled at the advertisement.

The backlash for the deleted video spilled over to other Instagram posts from both companies, where social media users continued to demand accountability and a more meaningful apology.

articles.title: Wyndham Clark addresses cheating allegations after being accused of improving lie during BMW Championship win
articles.summary: Wyndham Clark addressed the viral BMW Championship moment where he placed multiple irons behind his ball, defending the integrity of his actions.
articles.body: Wyndham Clark came under a bit of scrutiny during the final round of the BMW Championship on Sunday before stepping into the winner's circle. It's not the first time he's been caught in the crosshairs of golf fans, and he has learned from past experience that people will simply think what they want. After hitting his tee shot in the rough on the Par 4 14th hole at Bellerive Country Club, the CBS broadcast showed the two-time U.S. Open champion going through his pre-shot routine, which included him taking an iron out of his bag, placing it behind the ball, and taking a few practice swings next to it. Clark then went back to his golf bag, grabbed another iron, and placed it behind the ball. His caddie, David Pelekoudas, stepped between Clark and the camera while he made another practice swing before he went back to his bag for another iron. After the club changes and several times he sat his club behind the ball, CBS analysts Trevor Immelman and Frank Nobilo had a notable back-and-forth. "He’s taking a long look at this. This is like the third club that he’s placed down behind the ball there," Immelman said before Nobilo stated, "So the lie might be better." With the comments heard on the broadcast, coupled with golf fans on social media tossing around accusations, the moment became a major talking point on Sunday before Clark ultimately secured a three-shot victory. WHY WYNDHAM CLARK DESERVES PGA TOUR PLAYER OF THE YEAR, LIV GOLF'S FINAL HOORAH, AND SCOTTIE SCHEFFLER'S MONEY Clark was asked about the viral moment during Tuesday's news conference ahead of this week's Tour Championship, and explained that in no way did he approve his lie by placing multiple irons behind his golf ball. "I think any player, when they're trying to judge a lie, takes out different clubs to see what it feels like," Clark explained. I never fully put the club down behind it. I don't think anything of it. "When the cameras are on you, they're going to find anything. And I think you saw that in Bryson's case. It happened to me at the U.S. Open, it happened to me at Bay Hill. It's happened to a lot of guys where they can see stuff that maybe looks like something that maybe it's not. That lie was never bad. It was more just judging what it was. By no means did I take a bad lie and make it really good. "People can think what they want. I know I didn't do anything that was costing the integrity of the field. That's all I've got to say about that." Players are allowed to "ground the club lightly right in front of or right behind the ball," according to USGA Rule 8.1b(4). articles.title: PGA Tour Announces 2027 Schedule, Dates Revealed for Masters, U.S. Open, All Major Championships
articles.summary: The PGA Tour's 2026 season is set to come to an end this weekend with the Tour Championship, and the countdown to next year has already begun.
articles.body:
The PGA Tour's 2026 season is set to come to an end this weekend with the Tour Championship, and the countdown to next year has already begun.

On Wednesday, the PGA Tour announced its full 2027 schedule, running from Jan. 18 to Aug. 29. The schedule is highlighted by the major championship tournaments, including the Players Championship on March 8-14, the Masters on April 5-11, the PGA Championship on May 17-23, the U.S. Open on June 14-20 and the Open Championship on July 12-18.

In all, the 2027 PGA Tour schedule will feature 36 events, down just one from this year. There is one TBD event on the schedule that will run opposite the Genesis Invitational on Feb. 15-21.

The Sompo Championship on July 26-Aug. 1 is a new addition to the PGA Tour schedule and will serve as the penultimate event of the regular season. It will be followed by the GO by Raymond James on Aug. 2-8 before the 21st edition of the FedExCup Playoffs.

Though not on the official schedule, it was announced on Tuesday that NBA legend LeBron James is partnering with the PGA Tour to bring an event to his hometown of Akron, Ohio. The LeBron James Family Foundation Invitational will be played July 6-7 at the South Course at Firestone Country Club and will feature amateurs and pros from the tour's Pathway to Progression Pro-Bound Five program.

"The PGA Tour believes golf can create opportunity, change lives and bring communities together," PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said in a statement. "LeBron and the LeBron James Family Foundation have shown what is possible when that commitment is backed by action, and this partnership brings that shared vision to life. By connecting young people in Akron with our sport and supporting talented, up-and-coming athletes pursuing their dreams through our Pathway to Progression program, we are creating an event that honors Firestone's history and legacy while helping shape golf's future."

Before turning the page to 2027, 30 of the top golfers in the world will be vying for supremacy this weekend at the Tour Championship at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta.

articles.title: FedEx Cup Standings 2026, Points Leaderboard Before TOUR Championship
articles.summary: The top 30 golfers in the FedEx Cup standings are headed to East Lake Golf Club for the 2026 Tour Championship.
articles.body:
The top 30 golfers in the FedEx Cup standings are headed to East Lake Golf Club for the 2026 Tour Championship.

Scottie Scheffler was the runaway leader atop the points standings. He finished with a 1,523-point lead over Matt Fitzpatrick.

Once play begins at East Lake, though, points don't matter. The new Tour Championship format is a straight-up stroke-play event where the lowest score wins.

Bryson's lates post raises more LIV questions

Full standings can be found here on PGATour.com.

The 2026 Tour Championship has a new format than past years as the conclusion of the FedEx Cup Playoffs.

All 30 golfers in the field start at even-par and will play a 72-hole stroke-play event. The winner with the lowest score takes home the FedEx Cup.

In previous years, the leader of the FedEx Cup standings started at 10-under in a staggered scoring start.

The new format levels the playing field for all 30 golfers in the field and should make the weekend at East Lake more competitive.

The margin of victory in five of the seven years at the Tour Championship was three or more strokes.

Scottie Scheffler and Wyndham Clark come into East Lake as the winners from the last two weeks.

Clark might be viewed as the tournament favorite by some because of how well he played at the BMW Championship last week.

Rory McIlroy is also expected to be in the mix after he had a bounce-back week at the BMW.

Tommy Fleetwood is the reigning Tour Championship winner. He shot 18-under last year to claim the $10 million prize.

One other golfer to watch is Patrick Cantlay. He has four top-seven finishes at East Lake in his last four starts there. Cantlay finished second last week and enters East Lake with three straight top-12 finishes.

articles.title: Ryder Cup 2027: Luke Donald expects 'new faces' for Team Europe in 'very challenging' threepeat bid against Team USA
articles.summary: The British Masters marks the start of the year-long qualification process for Team Europe's 2027 Ryder Cup side; Luke Donald is looking to become the first captain to win three consecutive Ryder Cups; watch the Husqvarna British Masters live on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Donald led Team Europe to a 16.5-11.5 victory in Rome in 2023 and a historic 15-13 success on away soil at Bethpage Black last year, with the former world No 1 now looking to become the first captain to win three consecutive Ryder Cups.

The year-long qualification campaign for the 2027 European Ryder Cup team begins at the Husqvarna British Masters this week, live on Sky Sports , with Donald excited to seeing how his team evolves over the next 12 months.

"I always feel like when the qualification starts, it's sort of a reset for some of these players," Donald said. "Their goals change and suddenly they have an opportunity to earn Ryder Cup points and that's a pretty motivating thing for a lot of guys.

"Obviously this is my third crack [as captain], so I know a lot of the players. You are always going to have new talent coming up, and it's important to be around them and show some interest and keep them up-to-date in terms of how I see them playing.

"If they are playing some really good golf, and they have a chance, then it helps to be around them rather than just sending a text message."

Donald added in his press conference: "The home Ryder Cups feel more pressure. There's an expectation that you're meant to win and that brings its own pressure, then trying to win three in a row brings even more pressure.

"I think it's going to be a very challenging Ryder Cup, I honestly do. The home gives us a little bit of an advantage but the Americans are always very strong. Winning consistently in any sport, in anything, is very difficult."

Team Europe took 11 of their 12-man line-up and four of the five vice-captains from their 2023 victory to New York in 2025, with Rasmus Hojgaard replacing twin brother Nicolai as the only player change, but Donald expects differences in the 2027 team.

"I don't think we had ever had so many pass from one Ryder Cup to the next, same DNA - it was almost the same team," Donald admitted. "It was almost like 11 and a half people that we had.

"I expect there to be some new blood this time, and that's important. We were all rookies at some point as players and it's important to get out there - it's always easier a little bit for rookies to be at home. I expect the team to have a few new faces."

England's Marco Penge is among those chasing a Ryder Cup debut next September, having narrowly missed out on a captain's picks last time around despite three DP World Tour wins in 2025.

"I feel like I did as well as I possibly could [to qualify], but maybe experience was against me, which I totally understand why I wasn't [selected]," Penge said ahead of the British Masters. "Obviously Luke [Donald] made the correct decision with the way the team performed.

"There's loads of time to actually qualify and good golf will do the talking at the end of the day - that's what I've got to get back to. It's exciting to have something in the distance to push for."

Matt Wallace is another hoping to push for a debut spot, having narrowly missed out on being selected for the 2018 victory in France and a DP World Tour winner during the previous qualification campaign.

"It's probably my fourth campaign for a Ryder Cup charge," Wallace told the Sky Sports Golf podcast . "I've not made one yet but it's the biggest event I want to play in, outside of trying to win majors.

"If you make that team, you know you've made it properly. The picks nowadays that don't seem like it's left-field - it's people playing well, played well, past winners, major winners and things like that. If you make the team, you deserve to be there. "

Eligible DP World Tour members will be able to earn Ryder Cup points over the next 12 months, with the leading six players from the Ryder Cup Points list next August securing automatic spots. Donald will complete his line-up with six captain's picks later that month.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler Provides Health Update Ahead of Tour Championship After Revealing Illness
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler is getting back to full strength ahead of the 2026 Tour Championship this weekend at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta.
articles.body:
Scottie Scheffler is getting back to full strength ahead of the 2026 Tour Championship this weekend at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta.

After battling hand, foot and mouth disease during last week's BMW Championship and finishing tied for 12th, Scheffler sounds confident that he's on the mend.

"Good. I'd say I'm at like 95 percent," Scheffler said Wednesday, per ESPN's Mark Schlabach . "The only thing [is] maybe just still a couple of sores in my throat. But other than that, I feel really good."

According to the Mayo Clinic , hand, foot and mouth disease is a common viral illness that typically affects infant children, though it can be passed to people of any age. Symptoms can include a low-grade fever, sore throat, a rash on the palms of the hands and soles of the feet and painful lesions on the tongue, gums and inside the cheeks.

Before his disappointing finish at the BMW Championship, Scheffler kicked off the FedEx Cup Playoffs by winning the FedEx St. Jude Championship in Memphis by eight strokes. He revealed that he experienced pain while gripping his clubs at the beginning of the week before heading to St. Louis for the BMW Championship, where he finished 10 strokes behind winner Wyndham Clark.

Before he chases his second career win at the Tour Championship, Scheffler spoke about how family life can affect his play, as he and his wife, Meredith, have traveled with their two young sons, two-year-old Bennett and newborn Remy, to several tournaments.

"I think it's always a balancing act," Scheffler said. "I'm at a point in my life where, yeah, it's really hard having two young kids and taking care of them. I think anyone with young kids can relate; you're just tired literally all the time."

Despite the hardships of parenthood and his recent illness, Scheffler made it clear that he wouldn't change a thing.

"I think you want to enjoy the season because eventually my kids aren't going to be able to be out here," Scheffler said. "[Brian] Harman is somebody I talk a lot about this with. He's like, 'Man, I'm jealous of you guys who get to travel every week with your kids.' You take the good with the bad. Part of it is hard, but part of it is you've got to also enjoy it because it doesn't last."

articles.title: LIV Golf lays off majority of workforce
articles.summary: As its Saudi funding runs out, LIV will be laying off a substantial portion of its workforce.
articles.body:
LIV Golf as it's existed for the last five years — loud, brash, funded by billions from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund — reached its final conclusion at the end of its 2026 season last weekend. Now the organization is attempting to move on without Saudi funding, and the first effects of that transition are coming clear, starting with a substantial layoff of the majority of LIV Golf's workforce in the first week of September.

"The funding commitment announced by PIF earlier this year will reach its conclusion. As a result, we are scaling back operations as we transition to the next chapter of LIV Golf and work toward making LIV 2.0 a reality," a LIV Golf source said in a statement to Yahoo Sports. "This week, we informed many of our colleagues that their employment under LIV 1.0 will end in the first week of September. We are grateful to our employees for their hard work and dedication in building LIV Golf, and we remain committed to supporting those affected through this transition."

The PIF announced in April that it would be ending the funding of LIV Golf at the end of the 2026 season. LIV is now in the process of securing funding for future operations, though that is by no means certain. The proposed LIV Golf 2.0 would include 10 events for the 2027 season, five in the United States and five at international locations. LIV has already seen substantial success in international markets such as South Africa and Australia, drawing six-figure galleries.

The news that LIV will need to make substantial infrastructure changes comes as no surprise; the Saudi billions will be impossible to replace. LIV CEO Scott O'Neil has hinted at this reality in recent press conferences.

"This group has been under enormous pressure. We don't often control our destiny, and we are trying to do and be the best kind and type of people and partners that we built our careers on, our reputations on and our character on," he said. "We don't run, we don't hide. We just do what we can with what we have, and we're doing the best we can with that."

The transition to a LIV 2.0 model is expected to take months to finalize. While LIV officials are projecting optimism, and have hinted at the possibility of reinstating many of the employees affected by this layoff, substantial challenges to the league's future still exist.

articles.summary: RAJAHMUNDRY: Venkata Narasamamba Vasamsetty, the Indian-origin woman and US legal permanent resident who was detained by Immigration and Customs Enfor.
articles.body: RAJAHMUNDRY: Venkata Narasamamba Vasamsetty, the Indian-origin woman and US legal permanent resident who was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) despite having her immigration case dismissed by a judge has been granted bail by a federal court in Georgia, according to her family.Venkata, who hails from a village near Amalapuram in Konaseema district of Andhra Pradesh, was detained by ICE on August 11 after returning to the US following an extended stay in India. She has been a legal permanent resident of the US for nearly three decades and has held a green card since 2013.Venkata moved to the US in 1999 after her husband, who works in the software sector, had already settled there. She currently works as a teacher with the Wake County Public School System.Her family told TOI that she had frequently travelled to India to visit her ailing father, and alleged that her prolonged stays in India eventually led to her detention.The family expressed concern over what they described as the treatment meted out to Venkata following her detention.They alleged that she was handcuffed and transported in a closed van to a detention centre in Georgia, where, they claimed, the living conditions were poor.A family member also alleged that the prosecution strongly opposed Venkata's bail plea, while not opposing bail in eight cases involving Mexican nationals who had allegedly crossed the US border illegally.The family said they were concerned by what they perceived as differential articles.title: PGA Tour 2027 schedule: New event, big changes and different opening tournament part of revamped FedExCup calendar
articles.summary: The 2027 PGA Tour schedule will be the last of its kind before switching to a two-tiered model in 2028, Eight Signature events, a new California-based tournament and different venues feature in a 36-tournament calendar; watch the PGA Tour live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Eight Signature Events will feature in a 36-tournament schedule, with the season starting at The American Express in California from January 21-24 and finishing at the Tour Championship from August 26-29.

The only new addition is the Sompo Championship, which will be the penultimate event of the regular season from July 29-August 1, while the PGA Tour's Greensboro tournament has been rebranded from the Wyndham Championship to the GO by Raymond James.

A change to the Florida Swing sees The Cadillac Championship will now played from March 4-7 at Trump National Doral, the week before The Players, with the Arnold Palmer Invitational taking place from March 18-21 instead.

All other Signature Events remain the same and include the top 50 players from the previous year's FedExCup standings, as well as in-season qualifiers via the Aon Next 10 and Aon Swing 5.

The BMW Championship (August 19-22) shifts to Liberty National Golf Club in New Jersey, the site of the 2017 Presidents Cup and a venue that last hosted a FedExCup Playoffs event in 2019.

The 2027 FedExCup Fall schedule, along with eligibility criteria for the PGA Tour Championship Series and PGA Tour Challenger Series the following season, will be announced at a later date. The new structure for the season-ending Tour Championship will not be implemented until 2028.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler’s viral illness shows that not even the world’s best athletes are immune to the trials of parenthood
articles.summary: Professional athletes are often held up as something above and beyond the mere mortals who pay hefty ticket prices to be in the stands.
articles.body: Professional athletes are often held up as something above and beyond the mere mortals who pay hefty ticket prices to be in the stands. But every now and then there comes a reminder that even the best in the world at what they do can be waylaid by a universal experience. Just ask world No. 1 golfer Scottie Scheffler. The four-time major champion played below his usual standard in the opening round of last week’s BMW Championship outside St. Louis. He revealed after the tournament was over that he had been suffering from hand, foot and mouth disease – a familiar affliction to any parent with young kids. Scheffler said the painful sores associated with the viral illness made it hard for him to grip his clubs and nearly convinced him to withdraw from the tournament. A few days later, Scheffler described himself as at 95% with just a few sores left in his throat. The prospect of the world’s best golfer dealing with the same thing that so many parents experience is so humanizing for a player whose skill on the course might at times seem otherworldly. So, did Scheffler find it humbling? “Humbling is probably not exactly how I felt,” the Texan said, alluding to the frustration and pain he felt in Missouri. The 30-year-old Scheffler is a father of two – he and his wife, Meredith Scudder, have two sons: Bennett, 2, and Remy, who was born in March – and is in the prime of his career. The toddler ages are an incredibly intense period for any parent, but even more so for Scheffler and his family as they travel all around the country and he balances the life of a top professional athlete with being a father. It makes for a special life – Scheffler said other players tell him they’re jealous that he gets to have his family around all the time – but also a difficult one, especially for a player who appears to be the next legendary American golfer. “It’s always a balancing act. I’m at a point in my life where, yeah, it’s really hard having two young kids and taking care of them. I think anyone with young kids can relate, you’re just tired literally all the time,” he said. “I think you want to enjoy the season because eventually my kids aren’t going to be able to be out here. It’s something that I talked about with – (Brian) Harman is somebody I talk a lot about this with. He’s like, ‘Man, I’m jealous of you guys who get to travel every week with your kids.’ You take the good with the bad. Part of it is hard, but part of it is you’ve got to also enjoy it because it doesn’t last.” Other players can commiserate with Scheffler’s intense balancing act, particularly those playing at this week’s Tour Championship at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta where the best of the best play in the season-ending tournament. Rory McIlroy is another one of the world’s top golfers with a young child at home, though his 5-year-old daughter Poppy has moved out of the toddler stage. He said on Tuesday that the world’s best aren’t immune from the little indignities of parenthood, such as catching whatever illness they’re bringing home from daycare or school. “Kids bring stuff home from school. They bring stuff home from daycare out here. I think anyone that’s had children, it’s a part of it,” he said. “That’s the only way that they’re going to build up their own immunities. Unfortunately, the parents fall afoul of that at times. But that’s part of life. You’re going to get little viruses and little things that happen.” Gary Woodland, another Texan who often plays with Scheffler back in Dallas where they both live, said he’s never had hand, foot and mouth, but his kids – Jaxon, Maddox and Lennox – have had it twice. His assessment of the pain associated with the virus? “It is awful.” Scheffler’s decision to play through the painful sores is an example of what makes him great, Woodland said. “That’s the stubbornness that Scottie has, to fight through it last week and play,” Woodland said. “We all knew he was battling it. I don’t know if he came out with it until Sunday. We all have the same trainer, and we were trying to avoid the table he was working on. We were working on different tables and avoiding him at all costs. “One of (swing coach) Randy Smith’s big deals is making sure our grip is the same every day. One of the things we can control is controlling the club face and doing that and making sure our grip is the same. (Scheffler’s) got blisters on his hands and trying to grip the club. That just shows you how dang good he is to show up and finish 12th or however he finished last week. It’s impressive.” The determination – or stubbornness – to play through the blisters and sores is an example of what makes Scheffler such a great competitor and the mental strength required to be one of the best golfers in the world. It’s also a fine way to illustrate what he calls his “double life” that takes place on the course and off. The four-time major champion said when he’s inside the ropes at a tournament, he’s used to having everyone’s eyes trained on each move he makes. It’s a bizarre experience that professional golfers – particularly stars like Scheffler – have to thrive in, an experience that only athletes in solo sports can understand. It requires immense focus and incredible drive. Now compare that to how Scheffler describes what happens when he’s home with his family. “When it comes to going home, I just go home,” he said. He added, “I have my life out here where I play and compete, and I have my life at home where I don’t really do a whole lot, to be honest with you. It’s not that exciting. We have a great group of friends at home that I love to see. I’ve got great family. When I think about the fall and our offseason, we don’t really do a whole lot.” It’s a balancing act and a dichotomy that is incredibly hard to pull off for any parent, even if Scheffler can make it look so easy during big weekends on the PGA Tour. But every now and then, all it takes is a toddler passing along a virus to remind fans that even the most talented athlete is all too human.

articles.title: LIV Golf: Tyrrell Hatton expects league to continue next year despite job cuts
articles.summary: Tyrrell Hatton says he expects LIV Golf to continue next year despite confirmation of job losses.
articles.body:
Tyrrell Hatton says he expects LIV Golf to continue next year despite confirmation of job losses following the early conclusion of its season in Indianapolis last week.

The breakaway circuit that began in 2022 says it needs to find $350m (£257m) investment to survive.

LIV's season has finished early with the cancellation of its intended finale, this week's team championship in Detroit. Instead, Hatton is competing at the British Masters on Thursday.

"I would expect there to be LIV next season," the 34-year-old European Ryder Cup star told reporters at the Belfry, before news broke of the job cuts.

"I know they've worked really hard to get the funding stuff in place and its full steam ahead on that front."

Having lost the backing of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), LIV's future is under question. A term sheet has been signed with a potential new backer but with no confirmation that concrete funding is in place.

A LIV spokesperson has confirmed to BBC Sport that some employees are now being laid off.

"The funding commitment announced by PIF earlier this year will reach its conclusion. As a result, we are scaling back operations as we transition to the next chapter of LIV Golf and work toward making LIV 2.0 a reality," LIV said in a statement.

"This week, we informed many of our colleagues that their employment under LIV 1.0 will end in the first week of September. We are grateful to our employees for their hard work and dedication in building LIV Golf, and we remain committed to supporting those affected through this transition."

Amid such uncertainty, several LIV players have been linked with departing the tour, including Hatton. The Englishman chose Queen's I Want to Break Free as walk-on music in Indianapolis last week.

Asked by BBC Sport whether anything should be read into his seemingly provocative choice of song, Hatton said: "No. I've still got multiple years left on my contract with LIV and as I've said I've still got plenty of tournaments to play this year, so there is nothing really to focus on other than the golf."

Hatton will play the rest of the year on the DP World Tour, which will please European Ryder Cup captain Luke Donald, given that the qualifying period for the 2027 match starts this week.

While Hatton is publicly dismissing talk of jumping ship, there is still a strong feeling that he and team-mate Jon Rahm may have played their last events on the LIV tour.

If that is the case, Donald would welcome their full-time return to the DP World Tour. It would increase their chances of automatically qualifying for his team rather than having to rely on wildcard picks.

"You want to fill those six with the best," Donald told BBC Sport. "With someone like a John or Tyrrell playing more on the DP World Tour, they're going to have more opportunities to fill out those top six.

"And I think that's a good thing. You want your strongest players in those top six."

Donald also revealed that he had considered offering qualifying points to the LIV tour but the lack of clarity over the its future made it impossible.

"It was just too much uncertainty to think about giving them points for the Ryder Cup," he said.

Strained smiles and uncertainty - the strange end of LIV Golf 1.0

What now for Rahm, DeChambeau and LIV's biggest names?

Earlier this year the DP World Tour struck a deal with several LIV players, including Hatton and Rahm, to allow them to compete on the rival circuit without incurring sanction from the European-based tour. It meant they could remain members of the DP World Tour and therefore eligible for the Ryder Cup.

But that agreement only applies to this year and will not be available in 2027.

Hatton remains keen to maintain his position in the European Ryder Cup team.

"I've played the last four, they are extremely hard to make those teams," he said.

"Yeah, I'd be lying if I said I didn't want to be in every team possible moving forward."

This desire to represent Europe at Adare Manor in Ireland in September 2027 surely increases pressure on Hatton to leave LIV.

"I mean we still have to finish this season," he insisted.

"I'll essentially worry about that at the end of this season, but right now it is not really a thought process for me."

This will be another Ryder Cup qualifying period overshadowed by the LIV saga, as was the case in the previous two matches when Donald led Europe to victory in 2023 and 2025.

"I think every captain deals with a lot of challenges in the Ryder Cup," Donald said. "I think I've probably been the only one to deal with a changing landscape in golf.

"And it's been challenging at times, you know, it certainly has. But I think one of my strengths is just being very much in the present and having high standards for things that I can control and not really caring about things out of my control.

"Just dealing with them as they come. So, again, nobody knows what the future of LIV is going to be next year. Nobody knows which players are going to come and which are going to go.

"I try not to lose too much sleep about it, because it's just out of my control. Once it happens, then if I have an opportunity to change that, then I will. If not, I'm just going to go about my business."

articles.title: LIV Golf scaling back operations, terminating significant number of employees as funding expires
articles.summary: LIV Golf is set to scale back operations amidst the conclusion of its fifth season, the league announced Wednesday.
articles.body:
LIV Golf is set to scale back operations amidst the conclusion of its fifth season and expiration of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Funding, the league announced Wednesday. A significant number of the league's employees will be terminated the first week of September.

Golfweek confirmed the news with LIV Golf. SBJ was first to report LIV was scaling back operations.

"The funding commitment announced by PIF earlier this year will reach its conclusion," A LIV spokesperson said. "As a result, we are scaling back operations as we transition to the next chapter of LIV Golf and work toward making LIV 2.0 a reality. This week, we informed many of our colleagues that their employment under LIV 1.0 will end in the first week of September. We are grateful to our employees for their hard work and dedication in building LIV Golf, and we remain committed to supporting those affected through this transition."

LIV remains optimistic LIV 2.0 will happen, and the spokesperson confirmed with Golfweek that select employees will remain with the league to help guide it to its next iteration. The exact number of employees affected is unknown, and no decision has been made about how many employees may be able to return in the future.

The PIF announced in April it was pulling funding for LIV Golf following the 2026 season. Its reported losses are $6 billion. The league has had success in markets like Australia and South Africa, welcoming more than 100,000 fans to those events, but it hasn't caught on in the United States like it has in other parts of the world.

CEO Scott O'Neil shared earlier this month that a lead investor has signed a term sheet for at least $250 million to help build LIV 2.0. O'Neil has held multiple meetings with players in recent weeks to keep them informed of the next steps, which is likely to result in a 10-event schedule with reduced purses.

"I think about our evolution pretty simply," O'Neil said at LIV Golf Indianapolis. "In this next chapter is fundamentally different. We are building towards a league majority owned by its players, and I want you to think about just for a minute what that means. Players aren't simply playing for LIV Golf. They have an opportunity to own it."

Numerous players, including Jon Rahm, are still reportedly owed millions from their original contracts with the league, though the league is expected to give players equity in the new league to offset those figures.

"Ultimately, it's about building LIV into a sustainable sports business for the longer term," O'Neil said. "You might ask yourself why I'm so optimistic. I think the pieces are coming together right now exactly the way we'd hope. We have an ambitious lead investor with real resources, relationships and the belief and power of golf to think long-term."

But before LIV can get to its next chapter, it has to downsize from its first mission.

Cameron Jourdan is an assistant editor of Golfweek, covering college and amateur golf, the PGA Tour and plenty more. Follow Cameron on X/Twitter (@Cam_Jourdan) or Instagram (@GolfweekJourdan).

articles.title: Quail Hollow added to Championship Series as 2028 elite schedule starts to take shape
articles.summary: The Truist Championship at Quail Hollow Club is the latest tournament to be set for the top-tier Championship Series starting in 2028, another announcement t...
articles.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — The Truist Championship at Quail Hollow Club is the latest tournament to be set for the top-tier Championship Series starting in 2028, another announcement that was expected because the tournament has been elite since it began in 2003 and already is a signature event.

That makes eight tournaments announced for the Championship Series, the only two surprises being the new Sompo Championship and the Greensboro, North Carolina, event that has changed sponsorship and now is the GO by Raymond James .

PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said Tuesday that seven — now eight, with the Truist announcement Wednesday — of the 15 tournaments on the Championship Series have been announced. That doesn't include the four majors, The Players Championship and the postseason.

He said an additional three have been identified, and those will be disclosed shortly. There will be plenty of assumptions of current signature events, such as the AT&T Pebble Beach, the RBC Heritage and the Genesis Invitational.

The Genesis Invitational is the only player-hosted event — Tiger Woods — not yet announced. Part of that is due to the future of Riviera Country Club, which just finished a U.S. Women's Open in June, has the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and the 2031 U.S. Open. The private club might want a breather. Discussions are ongoing.

"Of the remaining four regular-season events, we are currently in active discussions with 14 prospective partners," Rolapp said. "Given that level of demand and interest, we expect to be making final decisions soon."

He said he expects to announce the full 2028 Championship Series schedule on Feb. 22 at a special television show from PGA Tour headquarters.

Jim Furyk is no longer just dipping his toes into the television world. The 2003 U.S. Open champion and two-time Ryder Cup captain has been named Golf Channel's lead analyst for PGA Tour events and the major championships.

Furyk agreed to a multiyear deal that takes him into the revamped 2028 schedule of Championship Series events. Golf Channel next year has full coverage of The American Express to start the season, and weekday coverage of the rest of the PGA Tour events (along with the U.S. and British Opens).

"I'm thrilled to expand my role with USA Sports and Golf Channel to call the action at men's majors and the biggest PGA Tour events for years to come," Furyk said. "I have really enjoyed my time in the booth and look forward to continuing to develop in the role."

The announcement would seem to end speculation about Furyk joining the NBC booth because Golf Channel and NBC are now separately owned.

The PGA Tour on Wednesday put out its full schedule for 2027, the last one before it changes to what amounts to a two-tour system .

It looks to be similar to this year, with a few tweaks. The Dallas-area tournaments are no longer in consecutive weeks in May. The CJ Cup Byron Nelson in Dallas will end in the first weekend of May, followed by the Valspar Championship in the Tampa Bay, Florida, area. That will lead into the Truist Championship, the PGA Championship and then Colonial will be the last week in May.

The Valspar previously was in March. That was been moved to clear the way for the Cadillac Championship in Miami to return to the Florida swing in March.

Also, the new Sompo Championship to be held in Napa, California, will be the last week in July and take the spot of the Rocket Classic in Detroit.

Pebble Beach again will have two events — the AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am in February and the U.S. Open in June. The British Open returns to St. Andrews and the PGA Championship is at its new headquarters in Frisco, Texas.

That means the Dallas-Fort Worth area will have three tournaments in five weeks — The CJ Cup Byron Nelson, PGA Championship and Charles Schwab Challenge at Colonial — with the PGA Championship and Colonial going back-to-back.

Colonial is about 50 miles southwest of Frisco.

Woodland still hearing about his tee shot

Gary Woodland is the feel-good story at East Lake simply by making it to the Tour Championship while trying to cope with the effects of his brain surgery three years ago.

That doesn't spare him from getting plenty of grief from last week at the BMW Championship .

He was on the bubble of being in the top 30, playing well in the final round at Bellerive, when he topped a tee shot into a creek about 100 yards in front of him on the ninth hole, leading to a double bogey. He was rock-solid the rest of the way, shot 69 and tied for fourth to advance.

He heard about it from Xander Schauffele on the putting green at East Lake on Monday. At the Payne Stewart Award ceremony Tuesday night, former award winner Brandt Snedeker was being interviewed on stage when he was asked if Woodland — one of Snedeker's assistant captains for the Presidents Cup next month — would be considered a captain's pick if he played well this week.

Snedeker paused during his answer, smiled and everyone knew what was coming. He mentioned the topped tee shot.

"I've hit some good shots this year, and I haven't got as much attention as that shot has," Woodland said.

Woodland even heard it from his father. They plan to play together again in December at the PNC Championship in Florida.

"When I turned my phone on after the round, it wasn't, 'Congrats' or 'Good playing.' It was: 'Hey, get that shot out of the way. I can't afford to have that in the scramble,'" Woodland said.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler shares a perfectly imperfect assessment of work-life balance, the challenges of fatherhood
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler opens up about the grind of raising two young kids while competing as the world's No. 1 golfer ahead of the Tour Championship.
articles.body: Scottie Scheffler is the No. 1-ranked golfer on Earth. He is also a husband and father to two children under the age of three. While that first fact about Scheffler is as unrelatable as they come, the second, the one that carries immense responsibilities and its own set of pressures, completely different from those he faces on the golf course, well, that's something millions can relate to. Being a professional athlete, and in Scheffler's case, being the literal best in your respective sport, while also being a family man and raising kids, is one of those things we regular folk can't comprehend simply due to the fact that so few people on Earth experience such a thing. SAM BURNS IS ONE OF AMERICA'S BEST GOLFERS, BUT FAITH, FAMILY AND THE USA MATTER MORE TO HIM THAN GOLF Every now and again, we're given minor glimpses into the personal lives of these all-world athletes that remind us that we're all just humans who actually do have shared experiences, and nothing humbles anyone on a more consistent basis than raising kids. For Scheffler last week, that humbling and relatable moment came in the form of hand, foot, and mouth disease. Following Sunday's final round in St. Louis, Scheffler revealed he had been battling the common childhood illness and the painful blisters that come with it throughout the BMW Championship. Speaking to the media ahead of this week's PGA Tour finale, the Tour Championship, Scheffler was asked if it was at all humbling that his life away from the course sometimes impacts his life inside the ropes. He took his time and delivered an imperfect answer, which, when it comes to talking about raising kids and a work-life balance, a perfect answer does not exist. "Humbling is probably not -- not exactly how I felt. I feel like I've talked a lot about like I don't -- like I have -- it's almost like a double life essentially," Scheffler began. "I have a life out here where I play and compete. When we're inside the ropes, it's definitely different than my home life. There's a lot of eyes on you. There's cameras like pretty much, let's say, six hours a day when I'm out here traveling...So when it comes to going home, I just go home, and I don't feel any different. I have my life out here where I play and compete, and I have my life at home where I don't really do a whole lot to be honest with you. It's not that exciting. "We have a great group of friends at home that I love to see. I've got great family. When I think about the fall and our off-season, we don't really do a whole lot. Like you said, striking the balance between competing out here while also traveling with my family is something that I'm always trying to strike the balance because I work really hard at my sport and I'm trying to be the best husband, father that I can be. "I think it's always a balancing act. I'm at a point in my life where, yeah, it's really hard having two young kids and taking care of them. I think anyone with young kids can relate, you're just tired literally all the time. "I think you want to enjoy the season because eventually my kids aren't going to be able to be out here. It's something that I talked about with -- (Brian) Harman is somebody I talk a lot about this with. He's like, 'man, I'm jealous of you guys who get to travel every week with your kids.' You take the good with the bad. Part of it is hard, but part of it is you've got to also enjoy it because it doesn't last." articles.title: Matt Gogel: US golfer gets six-month suspension for betting
articles.summary: American golfer Matt Gogel is suspended for six months for betting on golf tournaments.
articles.body:
American golfer Matt Gogel has been suspended for six months for betting on golf tournaments, the PGA Tour has said.

The 55-year-old competes on the PGA Tour Champions circuit which is reserved for professional golfers aged 50 and older.

Gogel did not bet on events in which he was participating but admitted to unknowingly violating PGA Tour policy by placing "small recreational wagers" in 2024 and 2025.

"I would never knowingly violate the integrity of the game of golf," Gogel said in a statement.

"I made an honest mistake and I look forward to playing in 2027 on the PGA Tour Champions."

He had two top-10 finishes across 18 PGA Tour Champions events in 2026 and was most recently in action during the Rogers Charity Classic in Calgary, Alberta where he finished tied 30th last week.

Gogel, who has earned more than $760,000 (£559,000) in prize money from Champions events, won the Pebble Beach National Pro-Am in 2002 - his only victory in 179 starts on the PGA Tour.

His suspension came into effect on 23 August and lasts until 22 February.

articles.title: LIV Golf lays off majority of staff as discussions continue to secure fresh investment and 'make LIV 2.0 a reality'
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) ended their funding for LIV Golf at the end of the 2026 season; LIV Golf has laid off most of their workforce while it looks to finalise investment to 'making LIV 2.0 a reality'
articles.body:
Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund [PIF] elected to end their funding after the conclusion of the 2026 season, with LIV Golf forced to reduce staffing levels regardless of whether they can finalise any potential transactions to continue.

The league informed 'the majority of its workforce' this week that their employment under LIV 1.0 will conclude early next month, having previously warned staff of potential redundancies in July.

No final decision has been made on the staffing levels required for any future version of LIV Golf, with the league - previously home to over 300 staff globally - still hopeful that some can return should the new iteration materialise.

"The funding commitment announced by PIF earlier this year will reach its conclusion," a LIV spokesperson told Sky Sports . "As a result, we are scaling back operations as we transition to the next chapter of LIV Golf and work toward making LIV 2.0 a reality.

"This week, we informed many of our colleagues that their employment under LIV 1.0 will end in the first week of September.

"We are grateful to our employees for their hard work and dedication in building LIV Golf, and we remain committed to supporting those affected through this transition."

The LIV Golf season finished a week early after the cancellation of the Team Championship in Michigan, with chief executive Scott O'Neil saying at their Indianapolis event he was optimistic they could finalise fresh investment and move forward.

LIV is understood to be in discussions with both a prospective lead investor and multiple minority investors, although the term sheet signed to fund them next season is non-binding and has not yet been finalised.

⁠Proposals include making the league majority-owned by its players and with a focus around 'commercial discipline', with a potential schedule of five Team Championships - in five different continents - and five Signature Events around the majors.

Bryson DeChambeau said ahead of last week's season finale he hoped people would give LIV Golf 'one more shot and be open minded', while Ian Poulter said it would be 'a real shame' if the league was unable to continue.

Tyrrell Hatton among the late entrants into the Husqvarna British Masters after the Team Championship cancellation, due to be held the same week, where the Englishman refused to be drawn into speculation over his own playing future.

"I would expect there to be LIV next season," Hatton said in his pre-tournament press conference. "I know they've worked really hard to get the funding and stuff in place, so I know it's full steam ahead on that front."

When asked whether he had considered his own future schedule: "To be honest, I haven't thought about that - I've got enough to worry about with playing golf for the rest of the year.

"I've still got multiple years left in my contract with LIV and I've got plenty of tournaments this year, so there's nothing really to focus on other than the golf."

articles.title: Good Good Golf and the high cost of an unfunny joke
articles.summary: In golf, one error can wreck an entire round. In advertising, one error can wreck an entire brand.
articles.body:
In golf, one error can wreck an entire round. In advertising, one error can wreck an entire brand.

One week ago, the YouTube golf/merch/lifestyle brand Good Good was flying high, its videos racking up hundreds of thousands of views, its merchandise for sale in major golf outlets nationwide, its logo soon to adorn an actual PGA Tour event. Now, thanks to an entirely unforced error, the brand is deep in the muck, everything it built at risk from an entirely unforced error.

Last Friday, Good Good and partner Callaway Golf released an ad that was supposed to use Good Good's personalities to promote a new Callaway driver. And in a case of careful-what-you-wish-for, everyone is indeed talking about the ad.

In the spot, Good Good personality Alexis Miestowski reaches toward a driver in a golf bag. Good Good's Garrett Clark then rushes over, knocks her to the ground, and growls as he looms over her, "Do not touch my driver."

The ad provoked immediate social media backlash for its depiction of violence against a woman, with many observers questioning how such an ad — which managed to be offensive, amateurish and unfunny — was even released in the first place.

"We posted a video to our channels that ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand. We have since taken that content down, and sincerely apologize," the brand said on Saturday morning . "Good Good has always stood for making the game of golf more inclusive for all, and we will continue to ensure that is our mission moving forward."

"We are disappointed by the content that was posted, and are appreciative of Good Good for addressing this. We look forward to working together to ensure a more inclusive space in golf," Callaway said in its own statement.

"The PGA Tour believes in golf's ability to bring people together and create a welcoming environment for all," the Tour added in its own statement. "We do not condone violence in any form, and the since-deleted video does not reflect our values or commitment to inclusivity and respect."

But unlike most social media pearl clutching, which dissipates before it breaks containment into the wider world, the heat on Good Good continued to rise even after the first round of statements. In his state-of-the-game press conference on Tuesday morning, PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp didn't give Good Good the benefit of the doubt. When asked whether he thought the brand had taken sufficient responsibility for the misfire of an ad, Rolapp responded, "I think initially, no. I think what we saw was concerning, is clearly not aligned with PGA Tour values. We take it very seriously. I think their initial response was disappointing. It was a bit defensive and late." He acknowledged that Good Good and Callaway had been taking some more positive steps, but the poor judgment and poor initial response, in the Tour's eyes, clearly linger.

The foundation began cracking under Good Good soon afterward. Golf retailer Golf Galaxy pulled out of a deal to sponsor a new iteration of the golf reality series Big Break co-branded with Good Good, and both Golf Galaxy and PGA Tour Superstore have yanked Good Good's merch off their shelves.

Now, the brand's sponsorship of the mid-November Good Good Championship in Austin, Texas, is under scrutiny. When asked directly about the brand's future with the tournament, Rolapp only described the situation as "fluid," offering no assurances whatsoever that the tournament's name was safe, a stunning potential fall for what had been, to this point, a true good-news brand story.

Until this controversy, Good Good epitomized grass-roots sports media success. Created in 2020 as a YouTube channel, Good Good has become a full-fledged multimedia lifestyle brand embodying golf course camaraderie. (The brand's name derives from mutual respect — "Good-Good" is a declaration you make in match play when you and your opponent are both close enough to the hole to call both short putts as made.)

YouTube golf influencers share a sport with the likes of Scottie Scheffler and Rory McIlroy, but not much else. The emphasis for YouTube golfers is on performance rather than technical skill, personality rather than steely perfection. And it's paid off; Good Good, with 2.1 million YouTube subscribers, is one of several golf influencer crews with seven-figure follower counts. (YouTube golf is such a compelling proposition that even LeBron James has joined the field .)

But as their profile grew, they morphed from social media influencers into a full-fledged brand. Now, they aren't only promoting themselves, but are being paid to promote their partners, which include Callaway Golf.

Good Good's ad, promoting a co-branded driver with Callaway, was apparently supposed to be a riff on the horror movie "Obsession," but the combination of awkward execution and reference to a cult-but-not-mainstream movie fell flat on the turf. Had Clark shoved one of the other male members of Good Good, the ad would've been like any other social media quick-hit video — flashing across phones for a day or so, and then forgotten. But with no one apparently able or willing to step in and say, "Hang on, maybe we shouldn't have a guy throwing a woman to the ground in this ad," Good Good is now in an existential crisis.

As with any social media pile-on, it's worth asking whether the punishment fits the crime. Does Good Good deserve to have its entire carefully built business torched because of one ill-advised ad? The problem here is that Good Good is playing in a space where image is everything, and where the sport is actively trying to work against its long history of misogyny and exclusiveness. The ad leaned into and reinforced the worst possible golf stereotypes and imagery. However this ends — and it's not looking good for Good Good — it's a true shame for Good Good's sake that no one thought to save them from themselves.

As anyone who's played golf knows, one bad shot at the worst possible time can tank your entire round.

articles.title: Anna Nordqvist: Three-time major winner and Europe Solheim Cup captain to retire
articles.summary: Three-time major champion Anna Nordqvist will retire from professional golf after this week's FM Championship near Boston.
articles.body:
Three-time major champion Anna Nordqvist will retire from professional golf after this week's FM Championship near Boston.

Nordqvist, 39, will captain Europe at Bernardus Golf in Netherlands, when they take on the United States on 11-13 September in the Solheim Cup.

The Swede has featured in each of the previous nine editions of the biennial contest, helping Europe lift the trophy on five occasions since making her debut in 2009.

That was the same year Nordqvist enjoyed her first major success at the LPGA Championship and she also triumphed at the Evian Championship in 2017 and the Women's Open in 2021.

In a post on social media, Nordqvist said: "Dear golf, 20 years ago, I came to the US with two suitcases, a golf bag and a dream of one day competing with the best golfers in the world.

"While my dreams never quite took me this far, I am very proud of myself for how far I've come and grateful for the dream I've been able to live ever since.

"I can't say it has always been easy, especially being so far away from my family, but they have supported me every step of the way. I've fallen so many times, but I never gave up, and I stood up every time I fell.

"I am forever thankful for everything this game has given me, and the people I have met along the way.

"I don't know how to say goodbye to something that means so much to me, but this is going to be the last week walking inside the ropes, competing on tour."

Nordqvist has earned $14.1m (£10.36m) during her 18-year professional career, that has included nine victories on the LPGA Tour and five on the Ladies European Tour.

While she is currently ranked 118th in the world, she finished in a tie for seventh in July's Evian Championship and was tied for 29th in the most recent Women's Open at Royal Lytham & St Annes.

Nordqvist had a benign cyst removed from her stomach during the summer of 2024, a year after her husband, Kevin McAlpine, died suddenly aged 39, while the couple were going through a divorce.

She added: "I'm not sure what the future has in store for me, but it's with a grateful heart I have decided to retire from playing professional golf to focus on my health and my family."

articles.title: Parrot eggs hatch in South Africa after suspected Thai smuggler arrested at OR Tambo airport
articles.summary: A 50-year-old Thai suspect was arrested with the eggs in a "homemade incubator" carried as hand luggage.
articles.body:
Fifty eggs suspected to be those of endangered parrots were intercepted at South Africa's main airport in Johannesburg last Thursday - and some of them have now hatched.

A 50-year-old Thai national was arrested for allegedly attempting to smuggle them in a "homemade incubator bag" carried as hand luggage, according to the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE).

Many of the rescued eggs have successfully hatched, with the chicks now receiving "intensive" care to "maximise their chances of survival", it added.

If convicted, the suspected wildlife trafficker faces a fine of up to 10m rand ($626,000, £461,000) or up to 10 years in prison, or both.

Initial investigations suggest the eggs belong to a parrot species protected under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (Cites).

The arrest followed a joint operation by the DFFE, the Green Scorpions - a specialised environmental enforcement unit - and various divisions of the police.

Environment Minister David Maynier has congratulated all the agencies involved, saying "illegal wildlife trafficking can only be challenged by a co-ordinated defence of our natural heritage".

He particularly thanked the dedicated staff at the National Zoological Garden in the capital, Pretoria, "who have been working tirelessly to incubate the seized eggs and provide specialised care to the hatchlings".

Last Thursday's arrest follows that of a 23-year-old Thai citizen in July, also caught at Johannesburg's OR Tambo International Airport, who was attempting to smuggle 418 parrot eggs.

The arrests highlighted the growing sophistication of transnational wildlife trafficking networks and reinforced "the importance of co-ordinated, intelligence-led law enforcement efforts", the DFFE said.

The illegal collection and trafficking of parrot eggs posed "a serious threat to wild bird populations and animal welfare", it added.

Officials explained that such eggs were often smuggled in improvised incubators and in conditions that endangered the welfare of developing embryos and hatchlings.

Wildlife trafficking remains a major threat in South Africa, one of the world's most biodiverse countries, with criminal networks frequently targeting animals such as elephants and pangolins, for sale on the international black market.

To combat the threat, the country adopted a new strategy six years ago to strengthen collaboration between government institutions, law enforcement agencies, conservation authorities, customs officials, prosecutors and international partners to dismantle criminal networks involved in the illicit wildlife trade.

articles.title: PGA Tour Suspends Matt Gogel for Betting on Golf Tournaments
articles.summary: The golfer, 55, played on the PGA Tour from 2000 to 2006
articles.body:
PGA Tour Champions golfer Matt Gogel has been suspended for betting

Gogel, 55, is suspended for six months, the PGA Tour said on Wednesday, Aug. 26

Gogel played on the PGA Tour from 2000 to 2006

PGA Tour Champions golfer Matt Gogel has been suspended for betting on golf tournaments.

The PGA Tour announced the suspension on Wednesday, Aug. 26 in a statement posted on X .

"Gogel placed bets on PGA TOUR competition but did not bet on tournaments in which he was a participant," the Tour said. "Gogel is suspended from PGA TOUR sanctioned competition for six months."

According to the Tour, Gogel's suspension began on Sunday, Aug. 23, and it is through Feb. 22, 2027.

"Gogel has cooperated fully with the TOUR throughout the process," the statement concluded.

In his own statement, Gogel confirmed the suspension — and said he "made an honest mistake."

"I want to be clear that these wagers were not placed on regular PGA Tour events, PGA Tour Champions events or any tournament in which I participated," Gogel, 55, said in his statement . "I would never knowingly violate the integrity of the game of golf."

He added, "I made an honest mistake and I look forward to playing in 2027 on the PGA Tour Champions."

Gogel turned pro in 1994 and earned his PGA Tour card in 1999 for the 2000 season. He competed on the tour for six years.

In 2002, he collected his first and only PGA tournament win at the AT&T Pebble Beach National Pro-Am.

His best finish at a major was in 2001, when he tied for 12th at the US Open.

After losing his tour card in 2006, Gogel transitioned to broadcasting, working for the Golf Channel and CBS Sports as a commentator.
